Forwarding Brightline’s ask and attachments. Quick internal notes below before we draft language:

- We can offer a limited carveout for a "transient performance cache" but must ensure:
  * Purpose limitation: only for request/response latency optimization and KV cache; expressly not for training, model improvement, analytics, or profiling.
  * Retention limit: 48 hours default; allow customer to request shorter SLA; automatic purge and zero durable backups beyond retention window.
  * Residency note: allow cross-region storage for cache nodes if customer consents and if data residency requirements (e.g., certain MA/CA health rules) are not triggered. For healthcare customers we should prefer onshore unless they explicitly accept risk.
  * Technical controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, isolated cache namespaces per customer, and periodic attestation audit for deletion.
  * Logging: we can provide deletion logs and cache audit events for the retention window; longer-term telemetry must be aggregated and pseudonymized.

I will draft proposed DPA/annex text and a short attestation addendum they can sign. Marissa/ Jonas — anything else from contract side?

Irene

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is proposed DPA annex language that addresses the security and residency concerns while allowing the operational cache you described. Please review and let us know if this meets Brightline’s compliance criteria; if so, we can prepare a short attestation/exhibit and execute via DocuSign.

--- Proposed DPA Annex: Transient Performance Cache
1) Scope and Purpose: Redwood may process Customer Data as a transient performance cache strictly for the purpose of request/response latency optimization and session-level KV caching ("Transient Performance Cache"). Customer Data stored in the Transient Performance Cache will not be used for model training, profiling, marketing, resale, or any purpose other than providing the agreed service.

2) Retention and Deletion: Data in the Transient Performance Cache will be retained for no longer than 48 hours by default. Redwood will implement automated deletion processes to ensure removal at the end of the retention period and will not retain backups of cache contents beyond the retention window. Customer may request a shorter retention period in writing at any time.

3) Residency and Transfers: Transient Performance Cache storage may occur in regions outside the Customer’s primary region solely to satisfy operational latency requirements, provided Customer expressly consents in writing to such transfers for cache nodes. Where applicable law or Customer policy mandates onshore-only handling, Redwood will provide an onshore-only cache configuration (subject to throughput/latency tradeoffs).

4) Technical Controls: Transient Performance Cache data will be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3). Caches are isolated by customer namespace and accessible only to runtime services required to serve requests.

5) Prohibitions and Auditability: Redwood will not use Transient Performance Cache data for training, profiling, advertising, or sale. Redwood will provide deletion logs and a cache audit report for the retention window upon Customer request and will include the carveout in security attestations.

6) Attestation: Upon execution of this annex, Redwood will provide a short attestation confirming compliance with the controls above and periodic evidence on request (within reason).

If this looks acceptable we can convert to an exhibit and send for signature (DocuSign link below).
